numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For `RegularGridInterpolator(..., method="linear")` on a degenerate 2D grid with single-point axes and float64 values, the call returns `array([nan])` instead of the numeric interpolated value. For the float32 variant shown, the result is `array([0.])` even though the float64 variant is `array([nan])`.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Return the correct interpolated value for the grid point input `[[0, 0]]` (i.e., not NaN).
trigger_conditions: 2D grid (points provided as two length-1 axes)
values provided as float64 for the 2D single-point case (values=np.array([[0]]) defaults to float64)
interpolating at xi=[[0,0]] (exactly the grid point)
oracle_clues: PR states that `RegularGridInterpolator` with `method=linear` works in the degenerate case of single-point grids, but that specifically for a 2D float64 grid a NaN is returned; the fix is to avoid returning NaN in that case.

The diff in `scipy/interpolate/_rgi_cython.pyx` shows that the branch which sets `out[point] = NAN` for the else-case (comment: "xi was nan") was removed/discarded, implying NaN should not be produced for this degenerate grid evaluation.

category_specific_evidence: The bug is for `interpolate.RegularGridInterpolator` with `method="linear"` on a 2D grid where both axes have length 1 (a single grid point).

Mathematical/functional property violated: in the degenerate case of a single grid point on both axes, linear interpolation should not produce an invalid value (NaN); it should return the grid value (`values[0, 0]`).
PR text: “BUG: interpolate.RegularGridInterpolator: fix linear interp. on 2D grid with a single point” and “However in the specific case of a 2D, float64 grid a Nan is returned.”

Concrete reproducer (float32 grid works, float64 grid fails as described):
`rgi = RegularGridInterpolator(points=([0],[0]), values=np.array([[0]], dtype=np.float32), method="linear")` then `rgi([[0,0]]) -> array([0.])`.

Code fix description: in `_rgi_cython.pyx`, it adds an explicit branch for `if grid[0].shape[0] == grid[1].shape[0] == 1: # single grid point along both axes: no interpolation` and sets `out[point] = values[0, 0]`.
Commit note: “As of 4c1a4da81 this fails for the parametrization `test_length_one_axes[linear-2-float64]`, but is OK in all other cases.”
reproduction_risks: Reproducer specifics for the failing case are only described indirectly (float64 2D length-1 axes); the provided explicit `In[8]/Out[9]` example uses float32 and returns `0.`.

The specific failing output value (NaN) is stated, but no explicit failing `rgi(...)` call with float64 is shown in the passages; reproduction must use the described conditions: 2D (`ndim=2`), `method="linear"`, dtype `np.float64`, and grid points with one element per axis.
Expected value and tolerance are not numerically specified; tests likely assert exactness but tolerance is not shown in the provided snippets.
